c.vcf.audio@init: The filter now takes oscillator 1. Turn FREQUENCY down to darken it and RESPONSE up to make it ring. The result is on row 10 at the filter LEVEL knob, so pin row 10 to an output (or to column D first, to give it an envelope).
c.vcf.noise@init: The filter now takes the noise generator. Turn FREQUENCY down to darken it and RESPONSE up to make it ring. The result is on row 10 at the filter LEVEL knob, so pin row 10 to an output (or to column D first, to give it an envelope).
c.vcf.fast@init: The filter now takes the fast LFO. Turn FREQUENCY down to darken it and RESPONSE up to make it ring. The result is on row 10 at the filter LEVEL knob, so pin row 10 to an output (or to column D first, to give it an envelope).

c.osc1.kbd@init: Oscillator 1 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts.
c.osc1.kbd2@init: Oscillator 1 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts.

c.osc2.kbd@init: Oscillator 2 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts.
c.osc2.kbd2@init: Oscillator 2 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts.

c.osc3.kbd@init: Oscillator 3 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts. Oscillator 3 is more sensitive than the other two, so the same INPUT LEVEL spreads its notes wider.
c.osc3.kbd2@init: Oscillator 3 now follows the keyboard: 0.08 semitones per key, so scales come out squeezed. FREQUENCY still sets where the keyboard starts. Oscillator 3 is more sensitive than the other two, so the same INPUT LEVEL spreads its notes wider.

c.decay.lfo@init: The LFO now lengthens and shortens each DECAY as it moves, so the envelopes ring for different lengths and, while the envelope repeats, come at an uneven pace.
c.decay.audio@init: Oscillator 1 now moves the DECAY time quickly, so each envelope falls in a ragged, uneven way.
c.decay.noise@init: The noise generator now moves the DECAY time quickly, so each envelope falls in a ragged, uneven way.
c.decay.fast@init: The fast LFO now moves the DECAY time quickly, so each envelope falls in a ragged, uneven way.
c.decay.env@init: The envelope now lengthens and shortens each DECAY as it moves, so the envelopes ring for different lengths and, while the envelope repeats, come at an uneven pace.
c.decay.kbd@init: Each note’s DECAY now depends on the key: higher keys give shorter notes.
c.decay.kbd2@init: Each note’s DECAY now depends on the key: higher keys give shorter notes.

c.revMix.lfo@init: The reverb comes and goes with the LFO: wetter as the voltage rises, drier as it falls.
c.revMix.audio@init: Oscillator 1 now moves the reverb MIX, so the amount of spring changes with it.
c.revMix.noise@init: The noise generator now moves the reverb MIX, so the amount of spring changes with it.
c.revMix.fast@init: The fast LFO now moves the reverb MIX, so the amount of spring changes with it.
c.revMix.env@init: The reverb comes and goes with the envelope: wetter as the voltage rises, drier as it falls.
c.revMix.kbd@init: The keyboard pitch now moves the reverb MIX, so the amount of spring changes with it.
c.revMix.kbd2@init: The upper voice now moves the reverb MIX, so the amount of spring changes with it.

c.lvl1.lfo@init: Tremolo: the loudness of output channel 1 rises and falls with the LFO. Pin a slow oscillator here and another to the other channel, a little out of step, and the sound swings between the speakers.
c.lvl1.audio@init: Oscillator 1 shakes the loudness of output channel 1 at audio rate: amplitude modulation, which adds ring-modulator-like overtones.
c.lvl1.noise@init: The noise generator shakes the loudness of output channel 1 at audio rate: amplitude modulation, which adds ring-modulator-like overtones.
c.lvl1.fast@init: The fast LFO now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 1: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.
c.lvl1.env@init: The envelope now moves the loudness of output channel 1. It swings negative while the envelope is up, so the channel gets quieter as each envelope rises and comes back as it falls: an upside-down envelope. Its resting voltage also opens the channel, so turn OUTPUT LEVEL down to compensate.
c.lvl1.kbd@init: The keyboard pitch now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 1: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.
c.lvl1.kbd2@init: The upper voice now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 1: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.

c.lvl2.lfo@init: Tremolo: the loudness of output channel 2 rises and falls with the LFO. Pin a slow oscillator here and another to the other channel, a little out of step, and the sound swings between the speakers.
c.lvl2.audio@init: Oscillator 1 shakes the loudness of output channel 2 at audio rate: amplitude modulation, which adds ring-modulator-like overtones.
c.lvl2.noise@init: The noise generator shakes the loudness of output channel 2 at audio rate: amplitude modulation, which adds ring-modulator-like overtones.
c.lvl2.fast@init: The fast LFO now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 2: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.
c.lvl2.env@init: The envelope now moves the loudness of output channel 2. It swings negative while the envelope is up, so the channel gets quieter as each envelope rises and comes back as it falls: an upside-down envelope. Its resting voltage also opens the channel, so turn OUTPUT LEVEL down to compensate.
c.lvl2.kbd@init: The keyboard pitch now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 2: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.
c.lvl2.kbd2@init: The upper voice now adds to OUTPUT LEVEL 2: a higher voltage opens the channel further, a lower one closes it.
